safeyard.label: Safeyard by Tirenify
safeyard.title: A free breach checker, built end to end.
safeyard.intro: Safeyard is the first product from Tirenify, the security company I founded in March 2026. You enter an email address. It checks a third-party breach database, shows what was exposed and tells you what to change first. No account is needed for the check.
lines: Tirenify is a digital security company for everyday internet users.
Safeyard is its first product, in public beta.
I build it alone and in public, and real user feedback decides what comes next.

shipped.title: Built the core check
copy: I connected the product to a third-party breach database, handled the response on the server and turned the result into plain language.
The check tells a person what was exposed and what to change first, without requiring an account.

shipped.title: Built weekly email monitoring
copy: A person submits an address and picks a day. A scheduled job checks it each week and emails the result through Resend, including a confirmation when nothing new is found.
I added practical tools and guides: password and PIN generators, a password strength checker and an email alias generator, plus guides on phishing, data breaches and WhatsApp security.

shipped.title: Built product analytics
copy: I track visits, completed checks and monitoring signups in Supabase.
Events are written only through a Postgres function. The table has row-level security and no public read access, so the browser can write events but can never read anyone else's.
A session ID and a campaign source tag from the URL tie each check back to where the visitor came from. A failed log call never blocks the check itself.
I found and fixed a double-counting bug caused by React StrictMode, and confirmed the fix on the deployed site.

shipped.title: Built and manage Tirenify
copy: I founded Tirenify in March 2026 and run product, positioning, feedback and early distribution as a solo founder and student.
I run a daily measurement routine: every link is tagged by source, and I review the results weekly.

shipped.title: Validated the product with real users
copy: I put Safeyard in front of beta testers and acted on what they said. I reworked the mobile navigation and the results layout within two days of a tester's report.

security.title: Security comes with the build.
security.intro: My main work is building products, websites and apps for businesses and startups. Security is the extra you get on top. Plenty of developers only build. I also check what I build for weaknesses, and that is the edge I offer.

applied.name: Secret handling
applied.text: The database service key stays on the server. I scan the built front-end files before each release to confirm no key has leaked into them.

applied.name: Row-level security
applied.text: Tables are locked down with row-level security. The browser can write analytics events but cannot read them back.

applied.name: Protected endpoints
applied.text: The scheduled monitoring job sits behind a secret bearer token and returns 401 without it.

applied.name: Input validation and rate limiting
applied.text: Email input is trimmed and validated on the server, and the monitoring signup is rate-limited per IP.

applied.name: Content Security Policy
applied.text: A CSP in the deployment config limits where the app can send data.

applied.name: Privacy by design
applied.text: The monitoring code does not log email addresses, and stored breach summaries are masked.

applied.name: Breach analysis
applied.text: I read breach records, map what was exposed to a severity rating, and turn it into plain steps a non-technical person can follow.

applied.name: Security awareness
applied.text: I write recovery guides and short lessons on phishing, data breaches and WhatsApp account safety.

extra.name: Vulnerability assessment
extra.text: I check your site or app for common weaknesses, starting with the OWASP Top 10, and tell you what to fix first. I only test systems you own or have authorised me to test.

extra.name: Log and alert review
extra.text: I know the basics of how security operations work: reading logs, triaging alerts and writing up what happened in plain language.

extra.name: Threat modelling
extra.text: Before I build a feature, I ask who would attack it and how, then design around the answer.

extra.name: Secure code review
extra.text: I review code for injection, broken access control and exposed secrets before it ships.

extra.name: Plain-language guidance
extra.text: I write short guides for your users or your team on phishing, passwords and account safety.

security.closing: I am not a full-time penetration tester or SOC analyst. I know enough to find the common problems, and I will tell you when something needs a specialist.

cards.title: You need the whole thing built.
cards.text: Front end, backend, database, auth and third-party APIs. I scope it, build it and hand it over. This is how I built Safeyard.

cards.title: You want to know what is weak before someone else finds it.
cards.text: A check of your site or app for common weaknesses: exposed keys, missing security headers, weak form and API handling, and risky dependencies. You get a plain-language report that says what to fix first. Add it to any build, or order it on its own. It is an assessment, not a full penetration test.

about.title: The honest version.
paragraphs: You have probably seen a lot of portfolios by now. I am not going to tell you I am the best at what I do. That would be a lie, and I would rather you hired me for the truth.

What I am is wide. I build products, websites and apps. I work on the front end, the back end and the database, and I look at security as well. I may not be the strongest at any one of those. What makes me a good fit for your project is that I adapt. I enjoy learning whatever a project needs, and if I do not know something yet, I will learn it and tell you while I do.

I'm Daniel. I am a self-taught developer based in Nigeria. I study Industrial Engineering at FUTA, I learned to code through The Odin Project, and I founded Tirenify in March 2026. I built Safeyard on my own.

I take on a small number of client projects alongside Tirenify. I work fast, I communicate clearly, and I do not take on work I cannot finish. If your project needs a specialist I am not, I will say so before we start.
